parameters.description: Specify the break duration, in seconds.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].costs
parameters.description: The `cost` attribute is used to define the cost of using the vehicle. It is a positive integer value with no specific unit of its own, but assumes the unit as per the value of `travel_cost` parameter. * When the `travel_cost` parameter is set to `distance` then `cost` will be in meters. * When the `travel_cost` parameter is set to `duration` then `cost` will be in seconds. * When the `travel_cost` is set to `customized` then `cost` will not have any unit, but during calculations it will be considered at its face value. * When the `travel_cost` is set to `air_distance` then `cost` will be in meters. `cost` parameter is critical in determining the number of vehicles to be used for optimization. The optimization engine will prefer using vehicles which help in lowering the cost for a particular route, if other parameters (location, time, etc) favor the configuration. Please note that: * When only the `fixed` vehicle cost is provided, it will be added to the `travel_cost` of the optimized route to arrive at the overall cost of the route. * When only the `per_hour` or `per_km` cost is provided for a vehicle, then the cost of the route to which the vehicle is assigned, is calculated using only the given `per_hour` or `per_km` cost and not the `travel_cost` of the route. * When `per_hour` or `per_km` is provided along with `fixed` cost for a vehicle, then the cost of the route to which the vehicle is assigned, is equal to the sum of `fixed` and calculated `per_hour` or the `per_km` costs. * `per_order` cost is always added to the overall cost of the route to which the vehicle is assigned.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].costs.fixed
parameters.description: Specify a fixed cost for using a vehicle. It should be a positive integer. Default value is 0.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].costs.per_hour
parameters.description: Define the cost for one hour of drive time of the vehicle. When `per_hour` cost is used, the final vehicle cost is determined based on the given value, instead of travel duration of the route. Please note that * `per_hour` cost is effective only when `travel_cost` is `duration`. Consequently, both `per_hour` and `per_km` can not be effective simultaneously for a given vehicle. * `per_hour` costs are ineffective when using `options.grouping` configurations.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].costs.per_km
parameters.description: Define the cost incurred by the vehicle for travelling a distance of one kilometer (km). When `per_km` cost is used, the final vehicle cost is determined based on the given value, instead of distance travelled on the trip. Please note that * `per_km` cost is effective only when `travel_cost` is `distance`. Consequently, both `per_hour` and `per_km` can not be effective simultaneously for a given vehicle. * `per_km` costs are ineffective when using `options.grouping` configurations.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].costs.per_order
parameters.description: Define the cost incurred by the vehicle for fulfilling one order. A job or a shipment, both are considered as a single order. When `per_order` cost is defined, the final vehicle cost is calculated as the sum of total costs of fulfilling the orders assigned to the vehicle and any other costs that the vehicle incurs (travel_cost, fixed cost, per_km or per_hour costs).

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].costs.min_stop_load_fixed_penalty
parameters.description: Specify the fixed penalty to be applied in case the vehicle is assigned to any delivery task with a load below the specified `min_stop_load` threshold. If all the tasks assigned to the vehicle have loads more than the specified `min_stop_load` threshold, this fixed penalty is not applied.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].costs.min_stop_load_unit_penalty
parameters.description: Defines the penalty applied per unit of load shortfall when a task’s load is lower than the vehicle’s configured `min_stop_load`. As a result, higher penalty values make the optimizer increasingly reluctant to assign low-load tasks to vehicles with higher minimum load expectations, while still preserving flexibility when capacity or feasibility constraints require such assignments.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].costs.deadhead_duration_penalty
parameters.description: Specify a penalty to be applied for each unit of deadhead duration exceeding the specified `max_deadhead_duration` for the vehicle. Default value is 0. Please note that this is ineffective when a `max_deadhead_duration` is not provided.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].costs.deadhead_distance_penalty
parameters.description: Specify a penalty to be applied for each unit of deadhead distance exceeding the specified `max_deadhead_distance` for the vehicle. Default value is 0. Please note that this is ineffective when a `max_deadhead_distance` is not provided.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].speed_factor
parameters.description: A positive number indicating the factor by which the vehicle’s speed should be adjusted , relative to normal speed, affecting the driving durations consequently. When `speed_factor` is greater than 1, effective travel time will be less than the normal travel duration. Similarly, when `speed_factor` is less than 1, effective travel time will be more than the normal travel duration. Please note that the `speed_factor` value supports values greater than 0 upto a maximum of 5.0, with a precision of two digits after the decimal point. For example, a normal trip duration of 1hr would be considered as a trip with duration of 30min if the `speed_factor` is 2. Using this attribute will have an effect on the vehicle’s arrival time at task locations (allocate task `time_windows` accordingly) and can affect the cost of the route as well (when `travel_cost=duration`).

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].layover_config
parameters.description: Use this object to configure continuous driving time limitations and subsequent rest duration for the driver. Please note that only one of `layover_config` or `breaks` is allowed for a vehicle, at a time.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].layover_config.max_continuous_time
parameters.description: Define the maximum time, in seconds, that a driver can drive without taking a break. This field is mandatory when using the `layover_config` attribute. Please note that accumulation of driving time is not interrupted by service time, setup or waiting time when fulfilling tasks, unless `include_service_time` is set to true. It is worth highlighting that, if different `max_continuous_time` durations are used then optimizer might choose vehicles with lower `max_continuous_time` because layover time is not affecting its objectives.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].layover_config.layover_duration
parameters.description: Specify the duration, in seconds, for which the driver should rest after driving continuously for the duration provided in `max_continuous_time`. This field is mandatory when using the `layover_config` attribute. Please note that the `layover_duration` will be added to the total service time and will impact arrival time of vehicle/driver at task’s location, but it won’t influence the `cost` or `duration` of the routes.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].layover_config.include_service_time
parameters.description: Choose if the optimizer should count the `service_time` spent while fulfilling tasks towards continuous working time of the driver. If set to `false` (default setting), only the driving time is considered to schedule the next break. When set to `true`, drive time and `service_time` are added together to determine the next break schedule.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].allowed_zones
parameters.description: Specifies the zones where the vehicle is allowed to fulfil any tasks. Please note the following: * If this parameter is provided, then the vehicle can fulfil tasks only in the given zones but, it is restricted from taking up tasks anywhere else. * Providing an empty array implies that there are no allowed zones. Consequently, the vehicle can only fulfill tasks without specified zones that are outside of any defined zone polygon boundaries. * If the parameter itself is not provided in the input, then the vehicle is allowed to complete tasks in all zones as well as outside them.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].restricted_zones
parameters.description: Specifies the zones where the vehicle is restricted from fulfilling any tasks. Although, the vehicle can be routed through such zones. Please note: * If this parameter is provided, then the vehicle is restricted from fulfilling tasks belonging to the given zones. Vehicle is allowed to fulfil tasks from everywhere else. * If an empty array is provided or if the parameter itself is not provided then zone based restrictions do not apply on the vehicle.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].max_distance
parameters.description: Specify the total distance, in meters, that the vehicle can travel. This is a constraint on the driving distance of the vehicle. In case `distance_matrix` is also provided in the input, then this constraint is applied on the distance driven as per the custom distance values instead of actual distance values.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].max_travel_time
parameters.description: Specify the total duration, in seconds, that the vehicle can be driven for. This is a constraint on the driving duration of the vehicle only and any wait, service or setup times spent towards the job is not counted against this constraint. In case `duration_matrix` is also provided in the input, then this constraint is applied on the drive duration as per the custom duration values instead of actual duration values.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].max_stops
parameters.description: Specify the maximum number of stops that the vehicle can make. Whenever the vehicle makes a stop during a trip, it is counted against the “max_stop” constraint. Vehicles stopping for breaks or layovers will not be counted against this constraint.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].profile
parameters.description: Specify the profile for this vehicle. The routing properties of the profile specified here must be defined within `routing.profiles` under `options`. If no profile is specified, then default routing profile is used.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].max_working_time
parameters.description: Specify the maximum duration, in seconds, that the vehicle can work for on the assigned route. Please note that all types of driver activities during the route—service, waiting, setup, and driving—contribute against the specified maximum duration.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].volume
parameters.description: Specify the dimensions of the vehicle's loading compartment. These inputs will be used to decide which cargo can be loaded into the vehicle based on their dimensions and alignment orientations. Please note that if a vehicle is not provided with the `volume` input, it can not be assigned to tasks with `volume` specified.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].volume.width
parameters.description: Compartment width, in meters.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].volume.depth
parameters.description: Compartment length, in meters.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].volume.height
parameters.description: Compartment height, in meters.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].max_depot_runs
parameters.description: Specify the maximum number of times the vehicle can return to the designated depot in order to reload items/cargo for completing additional tasks. Please note that: * `start_depot_id` is required for the vehicle when specifying `max_depot_runs`. * `relations` , `layover_config` , `depots.throughput` and deadhead constraints ( `max_deadhead_duration` and `max_deadhead_distance` ) can not be used along with `max_depot_runs.`

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].max_deadhead_distance
parameters.description: Specify the maximum distance, in meters, that the vehicle can accumulate as deadhead travel on a route. The scope for deadhead travel calculations is limited to only the first leg (start location / depot to first task location) and last leg (last task location to end location / depot) of the journey on any route. Following considerations apply on the deadhead calculations: * This is a soft constraint * In case of delivery type `jobs` the first leg will not be part of deadhead calculations as the vehicle carries the load to be delivered and hence, not traveling empty. Similarly, the last leg of the route will not be considered for deadhead calculations when pickup type `jobs` are present on the route. * For `shipments`, both the first leg journey and last leg journey be part of deadhead calculations. * `max_deadhead_distance` and `max_depot_runs` can not be used simultaneously.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].max_deadhead_duration
parameters.description: Specify the maximum duration, in seconds, that the vehicle can accumulate as deadhead travel on a route. The scope for deadhead travel calculations is limited to only the first leg (start location / depot to first task location) and last leg (last task location to end location / depot) of the journey on any route. Following considerations apply on the deadhead calculations: * This is a soft constraint * In case of delivery type `jobs` the first leg will not be part of deadhead calculations as the vehicle carries the load to be delivered and hence, not traveling empty. Similarly, the last leg of the route will not be considered for deadhead calculations when pickup type `jobs` are present on the route. * For `shipments`, both the first leg journey and last leg journey be part of deadhead calculations. * `max_deadhead_duration` and `max_depot_runs` can not be used simultaneously.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].min_stop_load
parameters.description: Specifies the minimum load threshold that should be preferred to serve at a stop. When a task’s load is lower than this threshold, the optimizer applies a penalty (as defined by `costs.min_stop_load_unit_penalty` and `costs.min_stop_load_fixed_penalty` ) instead of strictly rejecting the assignment. This allows users to discourage inefficient assignments for heavy vehicles by not assigning very light loads, while still keeping them feasible when no better alternatives exist. Please note that: * the number of elements in the `min_stop_load` array, should be exactly the same as those in the vehicle’s capacity input. * the `min_stop_load` threshold is effective only for “delivery” type `jobs`. * when multiple tasks are grouped together to share a single stop, the effective load used for `min_stop_load` calculations at that stop will be the sum of the loads of all tasks that are grouped. * if `min_stop_load` is provided without specifying the penalties `costs.min_stop_load_unit_penalty` and `costs.min_stop_load_fixed_penalty`), the stop load thresholds do not impact route choices.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].depot
parameters.description: **Deprecated! Please use the** `start_depot_ids` **and** `end_depot_ids` **to configure the originating and culminating depots for the vehicle, respectively.** The `depot` attribute specifies the ID of the depot that is assigned to the vehicle. Please note that if `depot` is specified, then the depot’s location will act as the starting point for the vehicle. There is no restriction on the number of vehicles that can be assigned to a depot but one vehicle can only have one depot.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.add[].max_travel_cost
parameters.description: **Deprecated! Please use the** `max_distance` or `max_travel_time` **parameters to limit the vehicle’s driving distance or driving durations respectively.** It restricts the maximum “cost” that a vehicle can incur while operating. This parameter is linked to `travel_cost` parameter, which determines whether the `max_travel_cost` value will be considered as `distance` (in meters) or `duration` (in seconds) or `customized`. For example, if the `travel_cost` attribute is set to `distance`, the `max_travel_cost` value will be considered as the maximum allowable distance that a vehicle can travel in the optimized solution. If the `travel_cost` parameter is set to `duration`, then the `max_travel_cost` value will be considered as the maximum allowable time that a vehicle can drive in the optimized solution. If the `travel_cost` is `customized` then the value provided for `max_travel_cost` will be compared directly with the custom cost of the route to determine if the vehicle can be assigned for that route or not. Please note that `max_travel_cost`, in this case, will be considered abstract (unit-less) and at face value. Setting a value for `max_travel_cost` ensures the vehicle does not exceed its operational limits, which can result in increased fuel costs, longer delivery times, or potential vehicle breakdowns.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.remove
parameters.description: An array of vehicle IDs to be removed when during re-optimization. All vehicle IDs provided must have been part of the original request.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify
parameters.description: An array of objects to collect the modified details of existing vehicles used in the original request. Each object represents one vehicle. Please make sure all the vehicle IDs provided here are same as the ones in the original request.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].id
parameters.description: Specify a unique ID for the vehicle. The IDs are case-sensitive.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].description
parameters.description: Specify a custom description for this vehicle. It will be returned in the response as-is.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].start_index
parameters.description: Specify the index of the vehicle’s starting point in the `location` array. The valid value range is \[0, length of `location` array). Please note that if either of the `start_index` or `start_depot_ids` is not provided, the vehicle starts from the location of the first task on its route.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].start_depot_ids
parameters.description: Specify the depots from which the vehicle can start. It is assumed that the vehicles can load the goods, which are to be delivered during the trip, when starting from the given depot. If certain delivery jobs can be serviced only by specific depots (`jobs.depot_ids`), then the vehicles starting from those depots only can fulfil such jobs. Jobs which do not have any pickup / delivery steps or do not have depots configured will be not impacted by setting this property. **Note:** * Pick-up type jobs which have depots configured, can not by fulfilled by vehicles who have only the start depots configured. * In case multiple depots are provided, then the vehicle starts from the depot which is nearest to the first task that it has to perform. * Please note that if either of the `start_index` or `start_depot_ids` is not provided, the vehicle starts from the location of the first task on its route.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].end_index
parameters.description: Specify the index of the vehicle’s final stop point in the `location` array. The valid value range is \[0, length of locations). Please note that if either of the `end_index` or `end_depot_ids` is not provided, the vehicle ends the trip at the location of the last task on its route.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].end_depot_ids
parameters.description: Specify the depots where the vehicle should end its trip. It is assumed that the vehicles will unload the goods, which were picked-up during the trip, upon arriving the given depot. If certain pickup jobs can be serviced only by specific depots (`jobs.depot_ids`), then the vehicles ending their trips at those depots only can fulfil such jobs. Jobs which do not have any pickup / delivery steps or do not have depots configured will be not impacted by setting this property. **Note:** * Delivery type jobs which have depots configured, can not by fulfilled by vehicles who have only the end depots configured. * In case multiple depots are provided, then the vehicle ends the trip at the depot which is nearest to the last task that it performs. * Please note that if either of the `end_index` or `end_depot_ids` is not provided, the vehicle ends the trip at the location of the last task on its route.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].capacity
parameters.description: `capacity` attribute is used to define multidimensional capacities of the vehicle. It is recommended to keep the dimensions of `capacity` consistent with the dimensions provided in quantity related attributes of `jobs` and `shipments` objects. Read more about the behavior of this attribute in the [Multi-Dimensional Parameters](#multi-dimensional-parameters) section.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].alternative_capacities
parameters.description: An array of alternate capacity configurations for the vehicle. Each array should have same number of dimensions as those configured when specifying task loads/quantities. Multiple arrays can also be specified to add more than one alternate capacity configurations for a given vehicle. These capacities can not be shared / merged. **Example:** An alternate capacity of \[ \[4,1\] , \[3,3\] \] indicates that the vehicle can either take 4 units of first dimension and a single unit of second dimension or else, 3 units each of both the dimensions.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].time_window
parameters.description: `time_window` field is used to describe the time period during which a vehicle is available to perform assigned tasks. The time_window should be specified in the format of \[start_timestamp,end_timestamp\] and each timestamp must be expressed as an UNIX timestamp in seconds. Please observe that it accepts only a single time window for the vehicle. It is important to note this difference with respect to the `time_windows` field used for `shipments` and `jobs`, which is a two-dimensional array used to describe the multiple time windows for each individual shipment or job.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].skills
parameters.description: It is a multi-dimensional object that can be used to define multiple skills and abilities of drivers or vehicles. Please note that only those vehicles with all the skills needed for a job/shipment will be assigned to fulfill that task. Read more about the behavior of this attribute in the [Multi-Dimensional Parameters](#multi-dimensional-parameters) section.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].max_tasks
parameters.description: Describe the maximum number of tasks that can be assigned to this vehicle. It should be a positive integer.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].breaks
parameters.description: The `breaks` attribute is used to provide details of breaks that a driver can take during their route. For each break, multiple time windows can be provided during which the break can actually be taken. Please note that: * All breaks are treated as mandatory by the optimization engine. If they are feasible, then all of them will be part of vehicle's trip. * Only one of `breaks` or `layover_config` is allowed for a vehicle at a time.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].breaks[].id
parameters.description: Specify an ID for the break. It should be a positive integer.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].breaks[].time_windows
parameters.description: Describe the possible time slots for the driver's break period to start. The time periods should be expressed as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. Please note that * Individual time window should not overlap with each other and should always follow the format of \[start_timestamp, end_timestamp\]. * All time windows of all breaks should be inside the vehicle's time window.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].breaks[].description
parameters.description: Add a custom description for the break.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].breaks[].service
parameters.description: Specify the break duration, in seconds.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].costs
parameters.description: The `cost` attribute is used to define the cost of using the vehicle. It is a positive integer value with no specific unit of its own, but assumes the unit as per the value of `travel_cost` parameter. * When the `travel_cost` parameter is set to `distance` then `cost` will be in meters. * When the `travel_cost` parameter is set to `duration` then `cost` will be in seconds. * When the `travel_cost` is set to `customized` then `cost` will not have any unit, but during calculations it will be considered at its face value. * When the `travel_cost` is set to `air_distance` then `cost` will be in meters. `cost` parameter is critical in determining the number of vehicles to be used for optimization. The optimization engine will prefer using vehicles which help in lowering the cost for a particular route, if other parameters (location, time, etc) favor the configuration. Please note that: * When only the `fixed` vehicle cost is provided, it will be added to the `travel_cost` of the optimized route to arrive at the overall cost of the route. * When only the `per_hour` or `per_km` cost is provided for a vehicle, then the cost of the route to which the vehicle is assigned, is calculated using only the given `per_hour` or `per_km` cost and not the `travel_cost` of the route. * When `per_hour` or `per_km` is provided along with `fixed` cost for a vehicle, then the cost of the route to which the vehicle is assigned, is equal to the sum of `fixed` and calculated `per_hour` or the `per_km` costs. * `per_order` cost is always added to the overall cost of the route to which the vehicle is assigned.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].costs.fixed
parameters.description: Specify a fixed cost for using a vehicle. It should be a positive integer. Default value is 0.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].costs.per_hour
parameters.description: Define the cost for one hour of drive time of the vehicle. When `per_hour` cost is used, the final vehicle cost is determined based on the given value, instead of travel duration of the route. Please note that * `per_hour` cost is effective only when `travel_cost` is `duration`. Consequently, both `per_hour` and `per_km` can not be effective simultaneously for a given vehicle. * `per_hour` costs are ineffective when using `options.grouping` configurations.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].costs.per_km
parameters.description: Define the cost incurred by the vehicle for travelling a distance of one kilometer (km). When `per_km` cost is used, the final vehicle cost is determined based on the given value, instead of distance travelled on the trip. Please note that * `per_km` cost is effective only when `travel_cost` is `distance`. Consequently, both `per_hour` and `per_km` can not be effective simultaneously for a given vehicle. * `per_km` costs are ineffective when using `options.grouping` configurations.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].costs.per_order
parameters.description: Define the cost incurred by the vehicle for fulfilling one order. A job or a shipment, both are considered as a single order. When `per_order` cost is defined, the final vehicle cost is calculated as the sum of total costs of fulfilling the orders assigned to the vehicle and any other costs that the vehicle incurs (travel_cost, fixed cost, per_km or per_hour costs).

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].costs.min_stop_load_fixed_penalty
parameters.description: Specify the fixed penalty to be applied in case the vehicle is assigned to any delivery task with a load below the specified `min_stop_load` threshold. If all the tasks assigned to the vehicle have loads more than the specified `min_stop_load` threshold, this fixed penalty is not applied.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].costs.min_stop_load_unit_penalty
parameters.description: Defines the penalty applied per unit of load shortfall when a task’s load is lower than the vehicle’s configured `min_stop_load`. As a result, higher penalty values make the optimizer increasingly reluctant to assign low-load tasks to vehicles with higher minimum load expectations, while still preserving flexibility when capacity or feasibility constraints require such assignments.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].costs.deadhead_duration_penalty
parameters.description: Specify a penalty to be applied for each unit of deadhead duration exceeding the specified `max_deadhead_duration` for the vehicle. Default value is 0. Please note that this is ineffective when a `max_deadhead_duration` is not provided.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].costs.deadhead_distance_penalty
parameters.description: Specify a penalty to be applied for each unit of deadhead distance exceeding the specified `max_deadhead_distance` for the vehicle. Default value is 0. Please note that this is ineffective when a `max_deadhead_distance` is not provided.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].speed_factor
parameters.description: A positive number indicating the factor by which the vehicle’s speed should be adjusted , relative to normal speed, affecting the driving durations consequently. When `speed_factor` is greater than 1, effective travel time will be less than the normal travel duration. Similarly, when `speed_factor` is less than 1, effective travel time will be more than the normal travel duration. Please note that the `speed_factor` value supports values greater than 0 upto a maximum of 5.0, with a precision of two digits after the decimal point. For example, a normal trip duration of 1hr would be considered as a trip with duration of 30min if the `speed_factor` is 2. Using this attribute will have an effect on the vehicle’s arrival time at task locations (allocate task `time_windows` accordingly) and can affect the cost of the route as well (when `travel_cost=duration`).

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].layover_config
parameters.description: Use this object to configure continuous driving time limitations and subsequent rest duration for the driver. Please note that only one of `layover_config` or `breaks` is allowed for a vehicle, at a time.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].layover_config.max_continuous_time
parameters.description: Define the maximum time, in seconds, that a driver can drive without taking a break. This field is mandatory when using the `layover_config` attribute. Please note that accumulation of driving time is not interrupted by service time, setup or waiting time when fulfilling tasks, unless `include_service_time` is set to true. It is worth highlighting that, if different `max_continuous_time` durations are used then optimizer might choose vehicles with lower `max_continuous_time` because layover time is not affecting its objectives.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].layover_config.layover_duration
parameters.description: Specify the duration, in seconds, for which the driver should rest after driving continuously for the duration provided in `max_continuous_time`. This field is mandatory when using the `layover_config` attribute. Please note that the `layover_duration` will be added to the total service time and will impact arrival time of vehicle/driver at task’s location, but it won’t influence the `cost` or `duration` of the routes.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].layover_config.include_service_time
parameters.description: Choose if the optimizer should count the `service_time` spent while fulfilling tasks towards continuous working time of the driver. If set to `false` (default setting), only the driving time is considered to schedule the next break. When set to `true`, drive time and `service_time` are added together to determine the next break schedule.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].allowed_zones
parameters.description: Specifies the zones where the vehicle is allowed to fulfil any tasks. Please note the following: * If this parameter is provided, then the vehicle can fulfil tasks only in the given zones but, it is restricted from taking up tasks anywhere else. * Providing an empty array implies that there are no allowed zones. Consequently, the vehicle can only fulfill tasks without specified zones that are outside of any defined zone polygon boundaries. * If the parameter itself is not provided in the input, then the vehicle is allowed to complete tasks in all zones as well as outside them.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].restricted_zones
parameters.description: Specifies the zones where the vehicle is restricted from fulfilling any tasks. Although, the vehicle can be routed through such zones. Please note: * If this parameter is provided, then the vehicle is restricted from fulfilling tasks belonging to the given zones. Vehicle is allowed to fulfil tasks from everywhere else. * If an empty array is provided or if the parameter itself is not provided then zone based restrictions do not apply on the vehicle.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].max_distance
parameters.description: Specify the total distance, in meters, that the vehicle can travel. This is a constraint on the driving distance of the vehicle. In case `distance_matrix` is also provided in the input, then this constraint is applied on the distance driven as per the custom distance values instead of actual distance values.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].max_travel_time
parameters.description: Specify the total duration, in seconds, that the vehicle can be driven for. This is a constraint on the driving duration of the vehicle only and any wait, service or setup times spent towards the job is not counted against this constraint. In case `duration_matrix` is also provided in the input, then this constraint is applied on the drive duration as per the custom duration values instead of actual duration values.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].max_stops
parameters.description: Specify the maximum number of stops that the vehicle can make. Whenever the vehicle makes a stop during a trip, it is counted against the “max_stop” constraint. Vehicles stopping for breaks or layovers will not be counted against this constraint.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].profile
parameters.description: Specify the profile for this vehicle. The routing properties of the profile specified here must be defined within `routing.profiles` under `options`. If no profile is specified, then default routing profile is used.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].max_working_time
parameters.description: Specify the maximum duration, in seconds, that the vehicle can work for on the assigned route. Please note that all types of driver activities during the route—service, waiting, setup, and driving—contribute against the specified maximum duration.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].volume
parameters.description: Specify the dimensions of the vehicle's loading compartment. These inputs will be used to decide which cargo can be loaded into the vehicle based on their dimensions and alignment orientations. Please note that if a vehicle is not provided with the `volume` input, it can not be assigned to tasks with `volume` specified.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].volume.width
parameters.description: Compartment width, in meters.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].volume.depth
parameters.description: Compartment length, in meters.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].volume.height
parameters.description: Compartment height, in meters.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].max_depot_runs
parameters.description: Specify the maximum number of times the vehicle can return to the designated depot in order to reload items/cargo for completing additional tasks. Please note that: * `start_depot_id` is required for the vehicle when specifying `max_depot_runs`. * `relations` , `layover_config` , `depots.throughput` and deadhead constraints ( `max_deadhead_duration` and `max_deadhead_distance` ) can not be used along with `max_depot_runs.`

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].max_deadhead_distance
parameters.description: Specify the maximum distance, in meters, that the vehicle can accumulate as deadhead travel on a route. The scope for deadhead travel calculations is limited to only the first leg (start location / depot to first task location) and last leg (last task location to end location / depot) of the journey on any route. Following considerations apply on the deadhead calculations: * This is a soft constraint * In case of delivery type `jobs` the first leg will not be part of deadhead calculations as the vehicle carries the load to be delivered and hence, not traveling empty. Similarly, the last leg of the route will not be considered for deadhead calculations when pickup type `jobs` are present on the route. * For `shipments`, both the first leg journey and last leg journey be part of deadhead calculations. * `max_deadhead_distance` and `max_depot_runs` can not be used simultaneously.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].max_deadhead_duration
parameters.description: Specify the maximum duration, in seconds, that the vehicle can accumulate as deadhead travel on a route. The scope for deadhead travel calculations is limited to only the first leg (start location / depot to first task location) and last leg (last task location to end location / depot) of the journey on any route. Following considerations apply on the deadhead calculations: * This is a soft constraint * In case of delivery type `jobs` the first leg will not be part of deadhead calculations as the vehicle carries the load to be delivered and hence, not traveling empty. Similarly, the last leg of the route will not be considered for deadhead calculations when pickup type `jobs` are present on the route. * For `shipments`, both the first leg journey and last leg journey be part of deadhead calculations. * `max_deadhead_duration` and `max_depot_runs` can not be used simultaneously.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].min_stop_load
parameters.description: Specifies the minimum load threshold that should be preferred to serve at a stop. When a task’s load is lower than this threshold, the optimizer applies a penalty (as defined by `costs.min_stop_load_unit_penalty` and `costs.min_stop_load_fixed_penalty` ) instead of strictly rejecting the assignment. This allows users to discourage inefficient assignments for heavy vehicles by not assigning very light loads, while still keeping them feasible when no better alternatives exist. Please note that: * the number of elements in the `min_stop_load` array, should be exactly the same as those in the vehicle’s capacity input. * the `min_stop_load` threshold is effective only for “delivery” type `jobs`. * when multiple tasks are grouped together to share a single stop, the effective load used for `min_stop_load` calculations at that stop will be the sum of the loads of all tasks that are grouped. * if `min_stop_load` is provided without specifying the penalties `costs.min_stop_load_unit_penalty` and `costs.min_stop_load_fixed_penalty`), the stop load thresholds do not impact route choices.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].depot
parameters.description: **Deprecated! Please use the** `start_depot_ids` **and** `end_depot_ids` **to configure the originating and culminating depots for the vehicle, respectively.** The `depot` attribute specifies the ID of the depot that is assigned to the vehicle. Please note that if `depot` is specified, then the depot’s location will act as the starting point for the vehicle. There is no restriction on the number of vehicles that can be assigned to a depot but one vehicle can only have one depot.

parameters.name: vehicle_changes.modify[].max_travel_cost
parameters.description: **Deprecated! Please use the** `max_distance` or `max_travel_time` **parameters to limit the vehicle’s driving distance or driving durations respectively.** It restricts the maximum “cost” that a vehicle can incur while operating. This parameter is linked to `travel_cost` parameter, which determines whether the `max_travel_cost` value will be considered as `distance` (in meters) or `duration` (in seconds) or `customized`. For example, if the `travel_cost` attribute is set to `distance`, the `max_travel_cost` value will be considered as the maximum allowable distance that a vehicle can travel in the optimized solution. If the `travel_cost` parameter is set to `duration`, then the `max_travel_cost` value will be considered as the maximum allowable time that a vehicle can drive in the optimized solution. If the `travel_cost` is `customized` then the value provided for `max_travel_cost` will be compared directly with the custom cost of the route to determine if the vehicle can be assigned for that route or not. Please note that `max_travel_cost`, in this case, will be considered abstract (unit-less) and at face value. Setting a value for `max_travel_cost` ensures the vehicle does not exceed its operational limits, which can result in increased fuel costs, longer delivery times, or potential vehicle breakdowns.

parameters.name: job_changes
parameters.description: This section gathers information on modifications to the number of jobs or their individual requirements for re-optimization. Any job from the original solution not specified here will be re-planned without alteration during the re-optimization process.

parameters.name: job_changes.add
parameters.description: An array of objects to collect the details of the new jobs to be added during re-optimization. Each object represents one job. Please make sure the IDs provided for new jobs are unique with respect to the IDs of the jobs in the original request.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].id
parameters.description: Provide an unique ID for the job. The IDs are case-sensitive.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].description
parameters.description: Add a custom description for the job.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].location_index
parameters.description: An integer denoting the index (in the `location` array) of the location coordinates where the job needs to be performed. The valid range of values is \[0, length of `location` array). Please note the `location_index` is mandatory when using the `jobs` object.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].delivery
parameters.description: In case the job involves a delivery step, use this attribute to describe delivery quantity. This attribute supports multidimensional quantities, to support delivering quantities of different units/dimensions. It is recommended to keep the dimensions of quantity for pickup/delivery consistent when defining them in `jobs` and `vehicles` (in `capacity` attribute). Please note that the quantity of delivery will be added to the assigned vehicle’s initial load. In case depots are being added, the delivery configured here can be fulfilled by vehicles starting from specific depots. Refer to `depot_ids` and `vehicles.start_depot_ids` to know more.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].pickup
parameters.description: In case the job involves a pickup step, use this attribute to describe pickup quantity. This attribute supports multidimensional quantities, to support picking up quantities of different units/dimensions. It is recommended to keep the dimensions of quantity for pickup/delivery consistent when defining them in `jobs` and `vehicles` (in `capacity` attribute). Please note that the vehicle will continue to carry the picked-up quantity until its last stop. In case depots are being added, the pickup configured here can be fulfilled by vehicles ending at specific depots. Refer to `depot_ids` and `vehicles.end_depot_ids` to know more.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].service
parameters.description: Use this attribute to define the time duration, in seconds, needed to complete the job. Default value is 0.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].time_windows
parameters.description: Define time periods within which this job should be started. The time periods should be expressed as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. Please note that the time periods should not overlap with each other and should always follow the format of \[start_timestamp, end_timestamp\].

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].skills
parameters.description: Define the skills needed to complete the job. This attribute supports multidimensional skills allowing users to add multiple skills. Read more about the behavior of this attribute in the [Multi-Dimensional Parameters](#multi-dimensional-parameters) section.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].priority
parameters.description: Specify the priority of this job. The valid values are in the range of \[0, 100\]. Default value is 0. Please note that setting a priority will only decide whether this job will be assigned or not, but has nothing to do with the sequence of job fulfilment.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].setup
parameters.description: Specify the job set-up duration, in seconds. `setup` is the one-time effort needed apart from working on the original task - for example, effort to record some information for compliance, or effort to set-up the equipment, or perform any other action for completing all steps required to fulfil the job. Please note that `setup` time is applied only once for a given task location. `setup` time, unlike `service` time, is not repeated in case there are multiple tasks at the same location.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].zones
parameters.description: An array of integers specifying the IDs of the zone(s) that this job belongs to. The job can be fulfilled by all vehicles which are allowed to complete tasks in the zone(s) assigned to this job. Please note following points about job zones: * If zone IDs are provided for any one of the jobs, then all other jobs should also be specified with zone IDs. Zone IDs provided here will override any zone geometries provided in the `zones` attribute and these IDs will be used for allocating appropriate vehicles. * Jobs can be auto-allocated to zones if this parameter is not specified while the zone geometries (either `zones.geometry` or `zones.geofence_id`) are provided. * If a job is located in an area where 2 or more zones overlap, it can be assigned to a vehicle permitted in _any_ of those zones. * Jobs not falling in any zones can be fulfilled by only those vehicles which are allowed to take up tasks outside zones as well. Refer to `vehicles` attribute for more information.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].depot_ids
parameters.description: Specify the depots which can be used to fulfil this job. In case of a pickup job, the assigned vehicle will deliver the goods to the depot specified here, at the end of its trip. Conversely, in case of delivery jobs, the vehicle will load the goods from the depot specified here, before starting the trip. **Note:** * If multiple IDs are provided for this field then any of the given depots can be used to fulfil the job. * If this field is not provided then the given job can be fulfilled by any vehicle (subject to other constraints configured in the input). * If the job does not have any delivery or pick-up step configured then depots configuration will not have any impact on the given job.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].load_types
parameters.description: Use this parameter to specify the type of loads for the given job. Once this property is configured, the job can not be served by a vehicle which has serviced any task whose load is incompatible with any of the`load_types` provided in this input. The load type considerations are ignored for the first task of the route. For example, an input value of \[“groceries”, “food”\] means that job’s load characteristics belong to either one or both types. Consequently, the optimizer will assign this job to a vehicle which has served other tasks whose `incompatible_load_types` do not contain either groceries or food. Note: * This parameter is effective only when a pickup / delivery is configured for the job. * If the job is part of any `relations` then, `load_types` might be ignored.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].incompatible_load_types
parameters.description: Use this parameter to specify the type of loads which are incompatible with the job’s load type. Once this property is configured, the job can only be serviced by a vehicle which has not serviced any other task with an incompatible `load_types` . Add multiple load types to indicate all the types which are incompatible for this job. The incompatible load type considerations are ignored for the first task of the route. For example, an input value of \[“groceries”, “food”\] means that current job’s load is incompatible with both groceries and food type of loads. Consequently, the optimizer will not assign this job to a vehicle which has served any task with `load_types` as either groceries or food. Note: * This parameter is effective only when a pickup / delivery is configured for the job. * If the job is part of any `relations` then, configured `incompatible_load_types` might be ignored.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].sequence_order
parameters.description: Use this parameter to prioritize completing a task relative to certain other tasks. A task configured with a `sequence_order` of 2 will be done after the task with `sequence_order` of 1, but before the task with `sequence_order` of 3. Valid range of values for this input is \[0,100\]. Please note that: * Only the tasks within the same route are compared and ordered as per their `sequence_order`. * Tasks without a `sequence_order` are not involved in the comparison. * Following is the precedence of `sequence_order` when used along side some of the other constraints: * `relations` are prioritized over `sequence_order` comparisons. * `sequence_order` will override `order_grouping` configurations.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].revenue
parameters.description: Specify the revenue earned by completing this job. The optimizer uses the `revenue` input to identify the potential profit earned by fulfilling this job after taking into account the costs incurred to do so. The`options.objective` and `vehicles.costs` input are taken into account to identify the costs of fulfilling the job. In general, the optimizer will prefer fulfilling the tasks with higher profits over the tasks with lower profits, should it need to reject some tasks in order to honor other constraints. In case the profit from fulfilling a job is negative, it will remain unassigned whatsoever.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].outsourcing_cost
parameters.description: Specify the cost of keeping this job unassigned, namely, the cost of outsourcing the job. When provided, the optimizer weighs the cost of assigning the job against the cost of keeping it unassigned and chooses a solution with lower cost. In the solution, the `outsourcing_cost` of unassigned jobs is added to the total cost of the solution. If the `outsourcing_cost` is not provided, which is to say that the job can not be outsourced, then the optimizer tries to fulfill the job irrespective of the cost incurred, subject to other constraints. Please note that `revenue` and `outsourcing_cost` can not be specified simultaneously for a job. Also, the `outsourcing_cost` would override the priority settings of the job.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].follow_lifo_order
parameters.description: Specify whether the job route should follow LIFO (last in, first out). Use this parameter when `pickup` or `delivery` jobs are involved and the loading or unloading sequence of cargo is important. The default is `false`.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].max_visit_lateness
parameters.description: It determines the allowable delay, in seconds, to begin a job after its designated time window has concluded. Please note that this parameter would override the `constraint.max_visit_lateness` (global) if both are specified.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].volume
parameters.description: Specify the dimensions and alignment configurations for the cargo associated with the task. These inputs will be used to arrange the items into the loading compartment of the vehicle to utilize the three-dimensional space. If a job consists of several different items, each with its own dimensions, please specify the final characteristics for the task: total height, total length, total width. Please note that vehicles which contain the `volume` input, will only be considered for arranging such items.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].volume.width
parameters.description: Cargo width, in meters.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].volume.depth
parameters.description: Cargo length, in meters.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].volume.height
parameters.description: Cargo height, in meters.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].volume.alignment
parameters.description: Refers to the orientation of the cargo in the loading compartment. It supports the following values: * **" "** : A blank space to indicate that the dimension check for the cargo should be skipped. This is also the default value. * **strict :** In this orientation, the cargo must fit within the vehicle’s dimensions exactly as is—no rotation is allowed. All dimensions of the cargo must be less than or equal to the corresponding dimensions of the vehicle. If any dimension exceeds that of the vehicle, the cargo cannot be loaded. * **parallel :** With parallel orientation, the cargo can be rotated around any one of the axes to help it fit into the loading compartment. For example, if the cargo is wider than the vehicle, it can still be loaded by rotating it around the vertical axis (so the width aligns with the vehicle’s depth) or the horizontal axis (so the width aligns with the vehicle’s height). Using this orientation, even a cargo whose one dimension is larger than the corresponding dimension of the vehicle but smaller than other dimensions, can also be loaded. * **fixed_bottom :** In this orientation, the cargo can only be rotated around the vertical axis, meaning its base stays fixed and it cannot be tilted or turned over. The height of the cargo remains aligned with the vehicle’s height and cannot be adjusted. As a result, if the cargo’s height exceeds the vehicle’s available height, it cannot be loaded into the compartment.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].joint_order
parameters.description: Specify a joint order group ID that this job is associated with. Tasks having the same joint order group ID are treated as a single unit: either all tasks in the group are assigned, or none are. Users can add tasks of both `jobs` and `shipments` types to a single joint order group by using the same unique ID. Please note that: * Each job in a single joint order group will be fulfilled by a unique vehicle. * Jobs belonging to a joint order group can be served in any sequence. * Joint order settings will not be effective if \`solution\` or \`relations\` attributes are also provided in the input request.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].split
parameters.description: An object to configure the rules for splitting the job into multiple sub-jobs. Please note that: * It is applicable only to `jobs` with: * a `delivery` or `pickup` quantity specified. * have only 1 load dimension (only element in the `delivery` or `pickup` array). Multi-dimension loads are not supported. * There is no partial completion for a splittable job - either all sub-jobs are fulfilled or none of them. * Each split part of the task is assigned a unique integer identifier in the range 0 ≤ identifier < total parts. These identifiers are available in the optimized result as `split_indicator`.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].split.can_be_split
parameters.description: Specify if a pickup or a delivery type job can be split into multiple sub-tasks. Default value is "false".

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].split.max_split
parameters.description: The maximum number of parts/sub-tasks that this job can be split into. This field is mandatory when `can_be_split = true` and must have a minimum value of 2.

parameters.name: job_changes.add[].split.quant
parameters.description: The minimum quantity allowed for each split sub-task, expressed as a ratio of the original job load (e.g., `0.25` ensures each split is ≥ 25% of the total). If omitted, the solver splits greedily based on available vehicle capacity. Please note that it is applicable only for tasks with single-dimensional load only.

parameters.name: job_changes.remove
parameters.description: An array of job IDs to be removed when during re-optimization. All job IDs provided must have been part of the original request.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify
parameters.description: An array of objects to collect the modified details of existing jobs used in the original request. Each object represents one job. Please make sure all the job IDs provided here are same as the ones in the original request.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].id
parameters.description: Provide an unique ID for the job. The IDs are case-sensitive.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].description
parameters.description: Add a custom description for the job.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].location_index
parameters.description: An integer denoting the index (in the `location` array) of the location coordinates where the job needs to be performed. The valid range of values is \[0, length of `location` array). Please note the `location_index` is mandatory when using the `jobs` object.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].delivery
parameters.description: In case the job involves a delivery step, use this attribute to describe delivery quantity. This attribute supports multidimensional quantities, to support delivering quantities of different units/dimensions. It is recommended to keep the dimensions of quantity for pickup/delivery consistent when defining them in `jobs` and `vehicles` (in `capacity` attribute). Please note that the quantity of delivery will be added to the assigned vehicle’s initial load. In case depots are being added, the delivery configured here can be fulfilled by vehicles starting from specific depots. Refer to `depot_ids` and `vehicles.start_depot_ids` to know more.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].pickup
parameters.description: In case the job involves a pickup step, use this attribute to describe pickup quantity. This attribute supports multidimensional quantities, to support picking up quantities of different units/dimensions. It is recommended to keep the dimensions of quantity for pickup/delivery consistent when defining them in `jobs` and `vehicles` (in `capacity` attribute). Please note that the vehicle will continue to carry the picked-up quantity until its last stop. In case depots are being added, the pickup configured here can be fulfilled by vehicles ending at specific depots. Refer to `depot_ids` and `vehicles.end_depot_ids` to know more.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].service
parameters.description: Use this attribute to define the time duration, in seconds, needed to complete the job. Default value is 0.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].time_windows
parameters.description: Define time periods within which this job should be started. The time periods should be expressed as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. Please note that the time periods should not overlap with each other and should always follow the format of \[start_timestamp, end_timestamp\].

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].skills
parameters.description: Define the skills needed to complete the job. This attribute supports multidimensional skills allowing users to add multiple skills. Read more about the behavior of this attribute in the [Multi-Dimensional Parameters](#multi-dimensional-parameters) section.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].priority
parameters.description: Specify the priority of this job. The valid values are in the range of \[0, 100\]. Default value is 0. Please note that setting a priority will only decide whether this job will be assigned or not, but has nothing to do with the sequence of job fulfilment.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].setup
parameters.description: Specify the job set-up duration, in seconds. `setup` is the one-time effort needed apart from working on the original task - for example, effort to record some information for compliance, or effort to set-up the equipment, or perform any other action for completing all steps required to fulfil the job. Please note that `setup` time is applied only once for a given task location. `setup` time, unlike `service` time, is not repeated in case there are multiple tasks at the same location.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].zones

Refer to `vehicles` attribute for more information.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].depot_ids

Conversely, in case of delivery jobs, the vehicle will load the goods from the depot specified here, before starting the trip. **Note:** * If multiple IDs are provided for this field then any of the given depots can be used to fulfil the job. * If this field is not provided then the given job can be fulfilled by any vehicle (subject to other constraints configured in the input). * If the job does not have any delivery or pick-up step configured then depots configuration will not have any impact on the given job.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].load_types
parameters.description: Use this parameter to specify the type of loads for the given job. Once this property is configured, the job can not be served by a vehicle which has serviced any task whose load is incompatible with any of the`load_types` provided in this input. The load type considerations are ignored for the first task of the route. For example, an input value of \[“groceries”, “food”\] means that job’s load characteristics belong to either one or both types. Consequently, the optimizer will assign this job to a vehicle which has served other tasks whose `incompatible_load_types` do not contain either groceries or food. Note: * This parameter is effective only when a pickup / delivery is configured for the job. * If the job is part of any `relations` then, `load_types` might be ignored.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].incompatible_load_types
parameters.description: Use this parameter to specify the type of loads which are incompatible with the job’s load type. Once this property is configured, the job can only be serviced by a vehicle which has not serviced any other task with an incompatible `load_types` . Add multiple load types to indicate all the types which are incompatible for this job. The incompatible load type considerations are ignored for the first task of the route. For example, an input value of \[“groceries”, “food”\] means that current job’s load is incompatible with both groceries and food type of loads. Consequently, the optimizer will not assign this job to a vehicle which has served any task with `load_types` as either groceries or food. Note: * This parameter is effective only when a pickup / delivery is configured for the job. * If the job is part of any `relations` then, configured `incompatible_load_types` might be ignored.

parameters.name: job_changes.modify[].sequence_order
parameters.description: Use this parameter to prioritize completing a task relative to certain other tasks. A task configured with a `sequence_order` of 2 will be done after the task with `sequence_order` of 1, but before the task with `sequence_order` of 3. Valid range of values for this input is \[0,100\]. Please note that: * Only the tasks within the same route are compared and ordered as per their `sequence_order`. * Tasks without a `sequence_order` are not involved in the comparison. * Following is the precedence of `sequence_order` when used along side some of the other constraints: * `relations` are prioritized over `sequence_order` comparisons. * `sequence_order` will override `order_grouping` configurations.

parameters.name: shipment_changes
parameters.description: This section gathers information on modifications to the number of shipments or their individual requirements for re-optimization. Any shipment from the original solution not specified here will be re-planned without alteration during the re-optimization process.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add
parameters.description: An array of objects to collect the details of the new shipments to be added during re-optimization. Each object represents one shipment. Please make sure the IDs provided for new shipments are unique with respect to the IDs of the shipments in the original request.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].pickup
parameters.description: Specify the details of the pickup step of the shipment.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].pickup.id
parameters.description: Indicate the ID of this shipment pickup step. An error will be reported if there are duplicate IDs for multiple shipment pick-ups. The IDs are case-sensitive. Please note `id` is mandatory when using the `shipments` attribute.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].pickup.description
parameters.description: Specify a custom description for the shipment pickup step.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].pickup.location_index
parameters.description: Indicate the index of the location for this shipment pickup. The index references the locations present in the `location` array. The valid range of value is \[0, length of `location` array).

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].pickup.service
parameters.description: Provide the time duration, in seconds, needed to complete the shipment pickup. Default value is 0.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].pickup.time_windows
parameters.description: Describe time periods within which the shipment pickup should be start. The time periods should be expressed as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. Please note that the time periods should not overlap with each other and should always follow the format of \[start_timestamp, end_timestamp\]

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].pickup.setup
parameters.description: Specify the set-up duration, in seconds, for the pickup. `setup` is the one-time effort needed apart from working on the original task- for example, effort to record some information for compliance, or effort to set-up the equipment, or perform any other action for completing all steps required to fulfil the job. Please note that `setup` time is applied only once for a given task location. `setup` time, unlike `service` time, is not repeated in case there are multiple tasks at the same location.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].pickup.sequence_order
parameters.description: Use this parameter to prioritize completing the shipment pickup relative to certain other tasks. A task configured with a `sequence_order` of 2 will be done after the task with `sequence_order` of 1, but before the task with `sequence_order` of 3. Valid range of values for this input is \[0,100\]. Please note that: * The shipment pickups's sequence order must be lesser than or equal to its corresponding delivery's sequence order. * Only the tasks within the same route are compared and ordered as per their `sequence_order`. * Tasks without a `sequence_order` are not involved in the comparison. * Following is the precedence of `sequence_order` when used along side some of the other constraints: * `relations` are prioritized over `sequence_order` comparisons. * `sequence_order` will override `order_grouping` configurations.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].pickup.max_visit_lateness
parameters.description: It determines the allowable delay, in seconds, to begin a shipment pickup after its designated time window has concluded. Please note that this parameter would override the `constraint.max_visit_lateness` (global) if both are specified.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].delivery
parameters.description: Specify the details of the delivery step for one-to-one type shipment. One to one shipments are those where the cargo is shipped from a pickup to a single delivery location.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].delivery.id
parameters.description: Indicate the ID of this shipment delivery step. An error will be reported if there are duplicate IDs for multiple shipment deliveries. The IDs are case sensitive. Please note `id` is mandatory when using the `shipments` attribute.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].delivery.description
parameters.description: Specify a custom description for the shipment delivery step.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].delivery.location_index
parameters.description: Indicate the index of location for this shipment delivery. The index references the locations present in the `location` array. The valid range of value is \[0, length of `location` array). Please note `location_index` is mandatory when using the `shipment` attribute.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].delivery.service
parameters.description: Provide the time duration, in seconds, needed to complete the shipment delivery. Default value is 0.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].delivery.time_windows
parameters.description: Describe time periods within which the shipment delivery should start. The time periods should be expressed as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. Please note that the time periods should not overlap with each other and should always follow the format of \[start_timestamp, end_timestamp\].

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].delivery.setup
parameters.description: Specify the set-up duration, in seconds, for the delivery. `setup` is the one-time effort needed apart from working on the original task- for example, effort to record some information for compliance, or effort to set-up the equipment, or perform any other action for completing all steps required to fulfil the job. Please note that `setup` time is applied only once for a given task location. `setup` time, unlike `service` time, is not repeated in case there are multiple tasks at the same location.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].delivery.sequence_order
parameters.description: Use this parameter to prioritize completing the shipment delivery relative to certain other tasks. A task configured with a `sequence_order` of 2 will be done after the task with `sequence_order` of 1, but before the task with `sequence_order` of 3. Valid range of values for this input is \[0,100\]. Please note that: * The shipment delivery's sequence order must be greater than or equal to its corresponding pickup's sequence order. * Only the tasks within the same route are compared and ordered as per their `sequence_order`. * Tasks without a `sequence_order` are not involved in the comparison. * Following is the precedence of `sequence_order` when used along side some of the other constraints: * `relations` are prioritized over `sequence_order` comparisons. * `sequence_order` will override `order_grouping` configurations.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].delivery.max_visit_lateness

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].deliveries
parameters.description: An array of objects to specify all of the delivery steps for one-to-many type shipment. One-to-many shipments ship the cargo from a common pickup location to 2 or more delivery locations over multiple steps. Please note that: * Each object in the `deliveries` attribute corresponds to one delivery step to be performed. * The order of individual deliveries in the optimized solution is determined by the optimizer subject to other constraints specified. * There is no partially completed shipment. Either all delivery steps of a shipment get assigned or none of them. When unassigned all steps of the given shipment `pickup` + `deliveries`) are listed under the `unassigned` attribute. * An error is returned if the number of delivery steps is less than 2. * Only one of `delivery` or `deliveries` is supported for any shipment. If both are provided, an error is returned.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].deliveries[].id
parameters.description: Unique ID of the shipment delivery step.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].deliveries[].location_index
parameters.description: Specify the index of location for this delivery. The index references the locations present in the `location` array. The valid range of value is \[0, length of `location` array). Please note `location_index` is mandatory when using the `deliveries` attribute.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].deliveries[].amount
parameters.description: Specify the quantity that needs to be delivered for this step. Multidimensional quantities, to support shipment of quantities of different units/dimensions, are also supported. Please note that: * The `shipments.amount` must be equal to the sum of the amounts of all individual deliveries. * All `deliveries[].amount` should match the dimensions of `amount`. The dimensions of `amount` and that of `capacity` in `vehicles` must be consistent. Read more about the behavior of this attribute in the [Multi-Dimensional Parameters](#multi-dimensional-parameters) section.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].amount
parameters.description: This parameter defines the quantity that needs to be shipped. This attribute supports multidimensional quantities, to support shipment of quantities of different units/dimensions. Please note that: * The dimensions of `amount` in `shipments` and that of `capacity` in `vehicles` must be consistent. * For one-to-one shipments (`pickup` + `delivery`), the `amount` indicates the quantity of the cargo to be transported. * In case of one-to-many shipment type (`pickup` + `deliveries`), the `amount` must be the sum of the amounts of all individual deliveries. Also, all `deliveries[].amount` should match the dimensions of `amount`. * The `amount` gets added to the assigned vehicle’s load. Read more about the behavior of this attribute in the [Multi-Dimensional Parameters](#multi-dimensional-parameters) section.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].skills
parameters.description: Define the skills needed to complete the shipment. This attribute supports multidimensional skills allowing users to add multiple skills for a shipment. Read more about the behavior of this attribute in the [Multi-Dimensional Parameters](#multi-dimensional-parameters) section.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].priority
parameters.description: Describe the priority of this shipment. The valid values are in the range of \[0, 100\]. Default value is 0. Please note that setting a priority will only decide whether this shipment will be assigned or not, but has nothing to do with the sequence of fulfilling shipments.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].zones

Refer to `vehicles` attribute for more information.

parameters.name: shipment_changes.add[].load_types
